 Fernando Cervantes Jr. USA TODAY Nov. 20, 2026, 1:31 p.m. ET Hear this story Toyota is recalling more than 60,000 vehicles over potential camshaft issues that could increase the risk of engine stall, according to a recent notice posted by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).
 According to the NHTSA, the recall covers certain Toyota truck models made from 2022 to 2023, as well as trucks made from 2025 to 2026. The recall stems from a camshaft issue that could cause the vehicles' engines to stall, increasing the risk of a crash.
 “One of the engine camshafts may have been manufactured incorrectly, allowing cracks to develop that can cause the camshaft to snap, possibly leading to an engine stall and loss of drive power,” the NHTSA said .
 Affected owners are expected to be notified by mail on Dec. 28. Dealers will inspect and replace affected camshafts, as necessary, free of charge. The recall covers 62,490 Toyota trucks.
 Here is what you need to know.
 What cars are affected by the recall?
 According to the NHTSA , the following cars are included in the ongoing recall:
 2022-2023 Toyota Tundra
 2025-2026 Toyota Tundra
